characterization_methods.key_findings: MHT effective grain size 7.31 μm; misorientation histogram dominated by a ~60° peak; proportion of special (Σ≤29) boundaries 71.2 %
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Chemically polished with colloidal silica without etching
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure effective grain size (twins included) by intercept lengths and quantify grain-boundary character (Σ≤29 special vs RHABs)

analytical_models.equation_role: decompose measured yield strength into strengthening contributions
analytical_models.model_note: σ_0, σ_GR and σ_PPT for S1000/S1050/MHT are similar in magnitude; the fine κ-carbide could not be quantified separately.

parameters.name: σ_PPT (precipitation strengthening, MHT, = σ_YS − σ_0 − σ_GR)

analytical_models.model_note: Coefficients/expression as printed; σ_0 = 97 + 279 wt% C + 1.5 wt% Mn + 20.5 wt% Al + 2.9 wt% Ni + 3.9 wt% Cr.
Hall–Petch slope K = 461 MPa μm^1/2 (from refs [12,43]); grain-boundary strengths of S1000/S1050/MHT computed as 145, 120, 63 MPa.

computational_details.simulation_method: analytical yield-strength summation (solid-solution + grain-boundary + precipitation strengthening)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The calculated contributions are used to explain the measured MHT yield strength of 910 MPa; the similar σ_PPT values among conditions are argued to explain why ductility/work-hardening are not significantly changed.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: crack deflection / zigzag cracking across special boundaries and twins
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: MHT has a larger number of special boundaries and larger grain size that impede dislocations from the crack tip; the crack paths constantly cross the special (low-energy) boundaries with constant deflection ('zigzag cracking'), increasing the effective crack-propagation length and energy dissipation (impact toughness +29 % vs S1050).

interfaces.interface_notes: Special (low-energy, Σ≤29) boundaries such as annealing twins and their variants provide lower interfacial energy and resistance to grain-boundary damage; in MHT they interfere with random high-angle boundaries (RHABs) and deflect propagating cracks.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Intergranular Cr7Cr3 precipitates present in S1000 dissolve during the 1050 °C stage of MHT; the intermediate 750 °C stage leaves closely spaced grain-boundary precipitates that increase twin nucleation sites; final state contains κ-carbide and B2 (B2 slightly smaller than in S1050). 71.2 % special (Σ≤29) boundaries are retained.

service_conditions.stress_state: uniaxial tensile loading and Charpy V-notch impact loading

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingot of nominal Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C–2Ni–3Cr (analyzed Fe-20.3Mn-8.6Al-1.4C-2.1Ni-2.9Cr wt.%) produced by vacuum induction melting; density 6.78 g/cm3.
Ingot homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h before hot rolling (shared fabrication step for the MHT sample).
Hot rolled at 1050–950 °C to produce a 6 mm sheet, followed by air cooling to room temperature.
First stage of the multi-stage heat treatment: 1000 °C for 3 min then quenched to room temperature.

processing_steps.method: secondary-stage heat treatment (MHT stage II, intermediate 750 °C treatment)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Intermediate stage: 750 °C for 15 min then quenched to room temperature. This stage produced many closely spaced grain-boundary precipitates (Fig. 9) that increased twin nucleation sites.
Final stage: 1050 °C for 3 min then quenched to room temperature, dissolving the intergranular Cr7C3 precipitates.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Room-temperature tensile and impact tests; tensile strength defined as maximum stress and yield strength as 0.2 % offset; properties are averages of three tests per condition
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Tensile: gauge length 25 mm, gauge width 4 mm, gauge thickness 5 mm, machined along the rolling direction; Impact: standard Charpy V-notch specimen 5 mm × 10 mm × 55 mm

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering and true stress–strain curves and strain-hardening-rate curves for MHT shown in Fig. 4(a,b) (MHT = black curve; MHT peaks slightly lower than S1000/S1050 and ends near ~50 % strain)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Coarser than S1000 (3.17 μm) and S1050 (3.84 μm)

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grains with annealing twins; matrix phase

phases_present.crystal_structure: co-gridded with austenite (superlattice reflections in SAED)
phases_present.morphology: nanoscale particles co-gridded with austenite; orientation relationship [011]γ//[011]κ

phases_present.grain_size: slightly smaller than the 20–160 nm B2 in S1050
phases_present.morphology: dark faceted particles within austenite grains

precipitates.distribution: nanoscale, co-gridded with the austenite matrix

structures.overall_structure: Fully austenitic matrix of equiaxed grains containing annealing twins; nanoscale κ-carbides co-gridded with austenite and a small amount of B2 particles; no intergranular Cr7C3 (dissolved by the 1050 °C final stage). Effective grain size 7.31 μm; 71.2 % special (Σ≤29) low-energy boundaries.

unmapped_findings: MHT Charpy impact: crack propagation energy = 36.78 J (vs 9.87 J for S1000 and 26.64 J for S1050); the crack initiation energy of MHT is comparable to S1000 and higher than S1050, and the fracture displacement is 8.04 mm.

Austenite composition of the MHT specimen measured by EDS (Table 2, wt.%): Mn 20.76 ± 0.61, Al 9.46 ± 0.33, Ni 2.01 ± 0.25, Cr 3.10 ± 0.57, C 1.15 ± 0.07, Fe Bal. (C calculated from lattice-parameter equations since EDS is unreliable for C).
Solid-solution strengthening of MHT from its austenite C content = 599 MPa; grain-boundary strengthening = 63 MPa; precipitation strengthening (σ_YS − σ_0 − σ_GR) = 248 MPa.
Impact fracture of the MHT specimen is fully ductile: dimples increase and microcracks disappear, with no quasi-cleavage plane observed (unlike S1000/S1050 which show quasi-cleavage and slip bands).
Tensile fracture of MHT shows shallower, more equiaxed and less developed dimples, consistent with a slightly reduced plasticity (TEL down 4.6 % relative to S1050).

The intermediate 750 °C/15 min stage of MHT produced many closely spaced grain-boundary precipitates (Fig. 9) that raised the stress in non-twinned regions, increasing twin nucleation sites and yielding more special boundaries that interfere with RHAGBs.
MHT retains a high proportion of special (Σ≤29) grain boundaries at 71.2 % (compared with 71.7 % for S1000 and 68.3 % for S1050), while intergranular Cr7C3 precipitates dissolve.
The 750 °C intermediate heat treatment did not significantly change the austenite chemistry relative to S1000/S1050 (Mn ≈ 21, Al ≈ 9, Ni ≈ 2, Cr ≈ 3.1–3.2, C ≈ 1.15–1.22 wt.%).
